- vsim moved to the external repo at /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim (the "hybrid_vsim" repo); there is NO verilator/ dir in andesim. Hybrid orchestration files live there under src/hybrid/*.hpp and cmake/HybridConfig.cmake.
- The VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID cmake option and the dmi_smoke/handoff_smoke targets were DELETED from the vsim repo in this session. HybridConfig.cmake now only registers the hybrid doctest unit tests (run via ctest / the check target). Any CLAUDE.md/USER_GUIDE text describing VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID must go or be rewritten to that reality. docs/USER_GUIDE.md around line 322 also mentions it — fix that too.
- scripts/hotloops.sh and tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotloops_*.sh are being DELETED this session; the hotloops tool is the C++ binary build/hotloops (source driver/hotloops.cpp), and the plugin builds via `make -C qemu_plugin` producing qemu_plugin/libhotloops.so. docs/hotloops.md must be updated: invocations `scripts/hotloops.sh ...` become `build/hotloops ...`; "plugin lives in contrib/plugins/, build with ninja -C build contrib-plugins" becomes "plugin lives in qemu_plugin/, build with make -C qemu_plugin". Read driver/hotloops.cpp's option parsing first and make sure every flag the doc shows actually exists in the C++ tool; if a documented flag does not exist in the C++ tool, delete that doc line and note it in your report.

Fix the section text (including numbered restore-order step 2/3 mentions of e8/m1) to match. Keep the edit minimal - correct the facts, do not restructure the section.

- QEMU is an external prebuilt at QEMU_BIN_DIR (config.env); nothing builds QEMU in-tree; setup.sh only validates externals and builds the qemu_plugin.
- docs/archive/ does not exist - remove dangling references per the findings.
- For docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb: it is raw JSON - edit the markdown cell source strings carefully and keep the JSON valid (validate with python3 -c "import json;json.load(open(...))" after editing).

Style rules: ASCII only (no em dashes, no curly quotes, no unicode bullets) for NEW text you write; do not touch content inside backticks unless it is the stale path itself; keep each file's existing tone and formatting; smallest edit that makes the text true.

When done: run `git -C /home/nick/work/andesim diff --stat` and report: per file, one line on what you changed, plus any finding you could NOT apply cleanly (content drifted, scope ambiguous) - do NOT force those, just report them. Your final message is data for me, not the user: keep it a compact list.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

/* Unified linker script for all hybrid test fixtures.
 *
 * Load base: 0x00100000 (1 MiB into andes_ae350 DRAM).
 *
 * andes_ae350 memory map:
 *   DRAM : 0x00000000 .. 0x7FFFFFFF  (writable, executable)
 *   MROM : 0x80000000 .. 0x87FFFFFF  (read-only)
 *
 * Reserved scratch (below text, used by .S fixtures):
 *   0x00000004              rt_csr_survival mtvec test value
 *   0x00001000              semihost_exit.inc param block
 *   0x00002000              rt_all_gprs spill area
 *   0x00003000              rt_mem_loadstore / rt_unaligned_lh buffer
 *   0x00010000              rt_shared_mem 4 KB buffer
 *
 * Layout above 0x00100000:
 *   .text         pinned at 0x00100000 (entry _start)
 *   .rodata
 *   .data         _edata terminates .data
 *   .bss          _end   terminates .bss (crt0 zeros [.bss, _end))
 *   _stack        0x00700000 (used by crt0.S to init sp)
 *
 * V-register transport scratch (L26): NOT a fixed address any more. The driver
 * maps one 4 KiB page above --mem-size and parks the scratch there (the mmap's
 * top page, v_scratch_gpa = ram_base + --mem-size), so it sits just past the
 * program's RAM -- nothing in this script can collide with it. No reservation
 * needed here.
 *
 * .S fixtures with no .data/.bss leave those sections empty (zero cost).
 * C fixtures rely on _edata / _end / _stack.
 */

ENTRY(_start)

SECTIONS {
    . = 0x00100000;

    .text : {
        *(.text.init)
        *(.text*)
    }

    .rodata : {
        *(.rodata*)
        *(.srodata*)
    }

    .data : {
        *(.data*)
        *(.sdata*)
    }
    _edata = .;

    .bss : {
        *(.bss*)
        *(.sbss*)
        *(COMMON)
    }
    _end = .;

    /* _stack sits well below V_SCRATCH (0x00FF0000) with ~9 MiB headroom.
     * Override at link time with -Wl,--defsym,_stack=... if needed. */
    PROVIDE(_stack = 0x00700000);
}

100	
101	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
102	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
103	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands, one write per register. Every CSR write -- the base M-mode scalars, the Andes V5 block, and the M-ext block -- also goes through Abstract Commands only, one write per CSR; there is no batched Program-Buffer sweep anywhere in the register/CSR transport, in either direction (a WARL/read-only CSR faulting mid-batch can't be tolerated the way the abstract path's per-CSR cmderr-clear can). `StateDrain` mirrors this: one abstract read per GPR/FPR/CSR. The Program Buffer carries only state the abstract command space cannot reach: the V-data sweep, `vtype`+`vl` (Tier B, see V-State Transport below), and the L2C MMIO window. **Liveness gate**: restores whose drained value equals the engine's own reset value are skipped (a no-op write; each DM op costs ~200-900 simulated cycles). The reset baseline is drained once per (engine build, ELF) on the first hybrid run and cached under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/`; `--no-reset-baseline` disables. Never gated: mstatus, GPRs, dpc, dcsr, mcycle, minstret, the S/U PMP mirror. Verify-transparent by construction (skip only when the value is already there).
104	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.
105	
106	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The QEMU plugin still drains `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) does not implement, so they are not restored -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record, deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
107	
108	**Privilege (L6)**: the handoff carries the real privilege level. The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). The `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` fixtures run on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (see `scripts/run_e2e.sh`); the ROI itself must still be trap-free, single-privilege, and paging-off (S-mode CSRs are not transported).
109	
110	### Trigger Modes
111	
112	The repo ships 2 switching modes (triggers); each measures one region you
113	choose. The C++ `andesim` driver exposes them via `--trigger marker|pc`.
114	
115	- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>` (`andesim_ROI_begin()/end()`).
116	- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; marker insns are bypassed. Both args are required.
117	
118	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc` is the unified orchestrator; `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. The run yields a cycle figure: window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`).
119	
120	### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
121	
122	`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr), (v3) the Andes V5 CSR block `struct hybrid_andes_csr andes`, (v4) the writable M-mode CSR block `struct hybrid_m_ext_csr m_ext`, and (v5) the L2C MMIO register window `struct hybrid_l2c l2c`. `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.
123	
124	**v3 Andes block**: `struct hybrid_andes_csr` carries the Andes-specific CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI -- 13 scalar CSRs (mxstatus, mpft_ctl, mclk_ctl, milmb, mdlmb, mecc_code, mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base, mcountermask_m, uitb, jvt, ucode) + PMA (pmacfg[2] @ 0xBC0/0xBC2, pmaaddr[16] @ 0xBD0..0xBDF). The 13 scalars are defined ONCE by the X-macro `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` in `state_abi.h`, which every consumer iterates (plugin drain, `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify) -- so adding a CSR is one line, no consumer drifts. Live only when `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` is set (the plugin sets it when QEMU's gdbstub advertised at least one Andes CSR). All restores are tolerant (a core lacking the CSR no-ops the write); the block round-trips through the trap-free ROI and is `--verify`-compared, except `msp_bound`/`msp_base` (HW stack-protection bounds) and `milmb`/`mdlmb` (ILM/DLM base+enable) which are engine-reset-divergent -- QEMU resets `msp_bound`/`msp_base` to all-ones (a vsim core without HW stack protection drains 0), and drains the `milmb`/`mdlmb` enable bit clear while the vsim RTL drains it set -- so they are verify-excluded like `mip`.
125	
126	**v5 L2C block**: `struct hybrid_l2c` carries the **L2 cache controller's MMIO register window** (`reg[]` = offsets 0x0000..0x0527, DS220 11.8.5 Table 112). Unlike every other block this is DEVICE MMIO, not a CSR: the plugin drains the whole window with `qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr` (physical address `l2c_base`, default 0xE0500000), and `ResumeDriver::restore_l2c` writes back ONLY the writable boot-static config registers -- Control (0x0008: `CEN` enable + prefetch + ECC + RAM timing), HPM Control (0x0010), Way Allocation Masks (0x0300..0x0328) -- via Program-Buffer word stores (`sw`, per DS220 11.8.3's <8-byte access rule). The read-only Configuration Register, the side-effecting CCTL command registers (writing one re-issues an L2 cache op), and the W1C error registers are captured but never restored. `StateDrain::drain_l2c` re-reads the config registers (`lwu`) for `--verify` (`state_diff` compares `l2c.ctrl` with the RO INITSTATUS[14] bit masked). This is the MMIO analog of the `mcache_ctl` (L1-enable) transport, and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. **Restore is HARD-gated on the engine having an L2C** (`Simulator::l2c_present()` from `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`): a store to an absent L2C region faults the Program Buffer, unlike a tolerant CSR write. Every current engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`, so the block is transported forward-looking and the restore/drain no-op today. QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register's reset value (`CEN=1`, DS220 11.8.7) at machine init (`andes_ae350.c`), so a guest that relies on the default is not drained as `CEN=0`.
127	
128	**v6 write-mask**: `write_mask[2]` (one bit per mask-governed config CSR, slot map + decode helpers in `include/hybrid/write_mask.h`, live under `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) records **which CSRs the guest actually WROTE** during the QEMU phase. The plugin decodes CSR-write instructions at translation time (`csrrw`/`csrrwi` always write; `csrrs/c` only when rs1!=x0; `csrrsi/ci` only when uimm!=0) and registers an exec callback only on instructions that write a mask-governed CSR -- steady-state code carries zero instrumentation, so the fast leg is unaffected. Consumers (`ResumeDriver` restore, `state_diff` verify) skip any governed CSR whose bit is clear: an untouched CSR's drained value is only QEMU's reset default, which can legitimately differ from the engine's RTL reset value (`msp_bound` all-ones vs 0, `milmb.IEN` 0 vs 1), so skipping keeps the engine at ITS OWN reset value -- what real silicon of that engine would hold -- and makes producer/engine reset divergence harmless by construction for every current and future engine, with no per-engine data in QEMU. Governed set: the v3 Andes scalars + PMA, the v4 M-ext block, `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`. Never governed: GPRs/FPRs/V, mstatus, dpc/dcsr, counters, fcsr, the trap-writable CSRs (mepc/mcause/mtval/mip/mie -- hardware writes them without a CSR insn), mtvec/mscratch, and PMP (the S/U mirror is a correctness requirement). `ucode` is transport-always (DSP ops set its sticky OV flag without a CSR insn). Flag clear (pre-v6 file) -> consumers fall back to restore/compare-everything.
129	
130	**Memory-content sidecars (NOT in `hybrid_state_v1`)**: ILM/DLM (`ROADMAP_ilm_dlm.md`) and HVM (`ROADMAP_hvm.md`) content travels OUTSIDE the state struct, as raw binary sidecar files next to each state file. The plugin (args `ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size` in bytes; bases default `0xA0000000`/`0xA0200000`/`0x90000000`) drains `<state>.ilm/.dlm/.hvm` through the slave-port/subordinate apertures; the vsim leg backdoor-loads them (`--ilm/--dlm/--hvm` -- zero-sim-cycle Verilator hierarchical-reference pokes into the RTL SRAMs, NOT the DM Program Buffer); the exit drain dumps the read-duals next to the handoff-out state. Armed by the engine's `--describe` sizes (`ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size`, bytes; 0 = no memory or wrapper lacks the set_*/get_* backdoor pair -- capability-gated so a config-has-it/wrapper-can't engine arms nothing). These QEMU memories are per-CPU overlays (LM) or standalone RAM (HVM), NOT backed by the shared mmap, so the sidecars are the only road their content travels; QEMU's raw geometry must be synced (`-readconfig` on the driver path, `-global` in tests/e2e.sh -- HVM's property is `hvm_size_pow_2`, log2) because QEMU's compiled-in defaults (2 MB ILM at 0x0, 1-BYTE HVM) are wrong for every engine.
131	
132	Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT`, `HYBRID_FLAG_L2C`, `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (in the external vsim repo).
133	
134	### V-State Transport
135	
136	V data registers (v0..v31) move through a scratch region in the shared mmap.
137	L26: that region is the mmap's TOP page, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) =
138	ram_base + ram_size - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`, NOT a fixed address. The driver
139	maps one page more than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes`), so the
140	scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size`, just above the program's RAM, where no
141	program layout can collide with it (`cmd_run` also rejects an ELF whose static
142	image would reach into it). `ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` take the GPA as a
143	required-when-V argument (the simulator passes `v_scratch_gpa()`); a V handoff
144	with it unset throws. vsim drives the transfer via the Debug Module **Program
145	Buffer** while the hart is halted, so benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
146	- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
147	  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
148	  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
149	- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
150	  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
151	  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` (the drained handoff file; there is no QEMU2 ship step).
152	
153	Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m1 (vl=vlenb), which also forces vstart=0 so
154	the unit-stride access covers the whole register. The scratch stride is the
155	compile-time `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` (wire-format per-register span), not the
156	runtime vlenb.
157	
158	V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
159	- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
160	- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)
161	
162	Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
163	1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
164	2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m1 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
165	   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
166	   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
167	3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
168	4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
169	5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
170	6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)
171	
172	`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
173	LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
174	sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.
175	
176	### Test Fixtures
177	
178	All fixtures run on the unified `tests/e2e.sh` harness, which
179	sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
180	the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. Three fixture families:
181	
182	| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
183	|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
184	| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
185	| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | hybrid round-trip tests, linked through the vplat runtime (below). Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- vsim resumes on QEMU1's memory, so the stack/heap and `main()`'s frame must survive the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. |
186	| vplat    | `vplat_hello`, `vplat_exit41`, `vplat_file`                 | smoke tests for the runtime's own features (exit code, file io). The runtime is engine-portable, shipped as `build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a` (sources in `runtime/`; build with `make -C runtime` or `scripts/build_all.sh runtime`): UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io, NO semihosting -- the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. Users link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. See docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`. |
187	
188	The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
189	then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.
190	
191	Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`; the shared runtime sources live at the repo root in `runtime/`. 1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands, one write per register. Every CSR write -- the base M-mode scalars, the Andes V5 block, and the M-ext block -- also goes through Abstract Commands only, one write per CSR; there is no batched Program-Buffer sweep anywhere in the register/CSR transport, in either direction (a WARL/read-only CSR faulting mid-batch can't be tolerated the way the abstract path's per-CSR cmderr-clear can). `StateDrain` mirrors this: one abstract read per GPR/FPR/CSR. The Program Buffer carries only state the abstract command space cannot reach: the V-data sweep, `vtype`+`vl` (Tier B, see V-State Transport below), and the L2C MMIO window. **Liveness gate**: restores whose drained value equals the engine's own reset value are skipped (a no-op write; each DM op costs ~200-900 simulated cycles). The reset baseline is drained once per (engine build, ELF) on the first hybrid run and cached under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/`; `--no-reset-baseline` disables. Never gated: mstatus, GPRs, dpc, dcsr, mcycle, minstret, the S/U PMP mirror. Verify-transparent by construction (skip only when the value is already there).
4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.

**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The QEMU plugin still drains `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) does not implement, so they are not restored -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record, deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

**Privilege (L6)**: the handoff carries the real privilege level. The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). The `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` fixtures run on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (see `scripts/run_e2e.sh`); the ROI itself must still be trap-free, single-privilege, and paging-off (S-mode CSRs are not transported).

### Trigger Modes

The repo ships 2 switching modes (triggers); each measures one region you
choose. The C++ `andesim` driver exposes them via `--trigger marker|pc`.

- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>` (`andesim_ROI_begin()/end()`).
- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; marker insns are bypassed. Both args are required.

`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc` is the unified orchestrator; `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. The run yields a cycle figure: window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`).

### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)

`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr), (v3) the Andes V5 CSR block `struct hybrid_andes_csr andes`, (v4) the writable M-mode CSR block `struct hybrid_m_ext_csr m_ext`, and (v5) the L2C MMIO register window `struct hybrid_l2c l2c`. `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.

**v3 Andes block**: `struct hybrid_andes_csr` carries the Andes-specific CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI -- 13 scalar CSRs (mxstatus, mpft_ctl, mclk_ctl, milmb, mdlmb, mecc_code, mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base, mcountermask_m, uitb, jvt, ucode) + PMA (pmacfg[2] @ 0xBC0/0xBC2, pmaaddr[16] @ 0xBD0..0xBDF). The 13 scalars are defined ONCE by the X-macro `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` in `state_abi.h`, which every consumer iterates (plugin drain, `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify) -- so adding a CSR is one line, no consumer drifts. Live only when `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` is set (the plugin sets it when QEMU's gdbstub advertised at least one Andes CSR). All restores are tolerant (a core lacking the CSR no-ops the write); the block round-trips through the trap-free ROI and is `--verify`-compared, except `msp_bound`/`msp_base` (HW stack-protection bounds) and `milmb`/`mdlmb` (ILM/DLM base+enable) which are engine-reset-divergent -- QEMU resets `msp_bound`/`msp_base` to all-ones (a vsim core without HW stack protection drains 0), and drains the `milmb`/`mdlmb` enable bit clear while the vsim RTL drains it set -- so they are verify-excluded like `mip`.

**v5 L2C block**: `struct hybrid_l2c` carries the **L2 cache controller's MMIO register window** (`reg[]` = offsets 0x0000..0x0527, DS220 11.8.5 Table 112). Unlike every other block this is DEVICE MMIO, not a CSR: the plugin drains the whole window with `qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr` (physical address `l2c_base`, default 0xE0500000), and `ResumeDriver::restore_l2c` writes back ONLY the writable boot-static config registers -- Control (0x0008: `CEN` enable + prefetch + ECC + RAM timing), HPM Control (0x0010), Way Allocation Masks (0x0300..0x0328) -- via Program-Buffer word stores (`sw`, per DS220 11.8.3's <8-byte access rule). The read-only Configuration Register, the side-effecting CCTL command registers (writing one re-issues an L2 cache op), and the W1C error registers are captured but never restored. `StateDrain::drain_l2c` re-reads the config registers (`lwu`) for `--verify` (`state_diff` compares `l2c.ctrl` with the RO INITSTATUS[14] bit masked). This is the MMIO analog of the `mcache_ctl` (L1-enable) transport, and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. **Restore is HARD-gated on the engine having an L2C** (`Simulator::l2c_present()` from `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`): a store to an absent L2C region faults the Program Buffer, unlike a tolerant CSR write. Every current engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`, so the block is transported forward-looking and the restore/drain no-op today. QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register's reset value (`CEN=1`, DS220 11.8.7) at machine init (`andes_ae350.c`), so a guest that relies on the default is not drained as `CEN=0`.

**v6 write-mask**: `write_mask[2]` (one bit per mask-governed config CSR, slot map + decode helpers in `include/hybrid/write_mask.h`, live under `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) records **which CSRs the guest actually WROTE** during the QEMU phase. The plugin decodes CSR-write instructions at translation time (`csrrw`/`csrrwi` always write; `csrrs/c` only when rs1!=x0; `csrrsi/ci` only when uimm!=0) and registers an exec callback only on instructions that write a mask-governed CSR -- steady-state code carries zero instrumentation, so the fast leg is unaffected. Consumers (`ResumeDriver` restore, `state_diff` verify) skip any governed CSR whose bit is clear: an untouched CSR's drained value is only QEMU's reset default, which can legitimately differ from the engine's RTL reset value (`msp_bound` all-ones vs 0, `milmb.IEN` 0 vs 1), so skipping keeps the engine at ITS OWN reset value -- what real silicon of that engine would hold -- and makes producer/engine reset divergence harmless by construction for every current and future engine, with no per-engine data in QEMU. Governed set: the v3 Andes scalars + PMA, the v4 M-ext block, `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`. Never governed: GPRs/FPRs/V, mstatus, dpc/dcsr, counters, fcsr, the trap-writable CSRs (mepc/mcause/mtval/mip/mie -- hardware writes them without a CSR insn), mtvec/mscratch, and PMP (the S/U mirror is a correctness requirement). `ucode` is transport-always (DSP ops set its sticky OV flag without a CSR insn). Flag clear (pre-v6 file) -> consumers fall back to restore/compare-everything.

**Memory-content sidecars (NOT in `hybrid_state_v1`)**: ILM/DLM (`ROADMAP_ilm_dlm.md`) and HVM (`ROADMAP_hvm.md`) content travels OUTSIDE the state struct, as raw binary sidecar files next to each state file. The plugin (args `ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size` in bytes; bases default `0xA0000000`/`0xA0200000`/`0x90000000`) drains `<state>.ilm/.dlm/.hvm` through the slave-port/subordinate apertures; the vsim leg backdoor-loads them (`--ilm/--dlm/--hvm` -- zero-sim-cycle Verilator hierarchical-reference pokes into the RTL SRAMs, NOT the DM Program Buffer); the exit drain dumps the read-duals next to the handoff-out state. Armed by the engine's `--describe` sizes (`ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size`, bytes; 0 = no memory or wrapper lacks the set_*/get_* backdoor pair -- capability-gated so a config-has-it/wrapper-can't engine arms nothing). These QEMU memories are per-CPU overlays (LM) or standalone RAM (HVM), NOT backed by the shared mmap, so the sidecars are the only road their content travels; QEMU's raw geometry must be synced (`-readconfig` on the driver path, `-global` in tests/e2e.sh -- HVM's property is `hvm_size_pow_2`, log2) because QEMU's compiled-in defaults (2 MB ILM at 0x0, 1-BYTE HVM) are wrong for every engine.

Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT`, `HYBRID_FLAG_L2C`, `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (in the external vsim repo).

### V-State Transport

V data registers (v0..v31) move through a scratch region in the shared mmap.
L26: that region is the mmap's TOP page, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) =
ram_base + ram_size - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`, NOT a fixed address. The driver
maps one page more than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes`), so the
scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size`, just above the program's RAM, where no
program layout can collide with it (`cmd_run` also rejects an ELF whose static
image would reach into it). `ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` take the GPA as a
required-when-V argument (the simulator passes `v_scratch_gpa()`); a V handoff
with it unset throws. vsim drives the transfer via the Debug Module **Program
Buffer** while the hart is halted, so benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` (the drained handoff file; there is no QEMU2 ship step).

Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m1 (vl=vlenb), which also forces vstart=0 so
the unit-stride access covers the whole register. The scratch stride is the
compile-time `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` (wire-format per-register span), not the
runtime vlenb.

V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)

Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m1 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)

`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.

### Test Fixtures

All fixtures run on the unified `tests/e2e.sh` harness, which
sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. Three fixture families:

| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | hybrid round-trip tests, linked through the vplat runtime (below). Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- vsim resumes on QEMU1's memory, so the stack/heap and `main()`'s frame must survive the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. |
| vplat    | `vplat_hello`, `vplat_exit41`, `vplat_file`                 | smoke tests for the runtime's own features (exit code, file io). The runtime is engine-portable, shipped as `build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a` (sources in `runtime/`; build with `make -C runtime` or `scripts/build_all.sh runtime`): UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io, NO semihosting -- the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. Users link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. See docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`. |

The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.

Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`; the shared runtime sources live at the repo root in `runtime/`. ALL C fixtures (rt_c_* and vplat_*) link through the shipped vplat runtime with the user command (`-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`); nothing in-tree links `-lgloss_vh` or uses semihosting syscalls anymore (asm fixtures still carry a semihosting exit fallback from `semihost_exit.inc`). V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. Syscalls bottom out in MMIO devices both engines model (UART2 `0xf0300000`, SimControl/HTIF `0xe0080000` -- QEMU side is inline in `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c`), so a `printf` inside the ROI works on every engine (it just adds the real UART cycles to the figure); the old "Phase-2 no-syscall rule" survives only as a measurement-hygiene convention in cycle-measuring fixtures, and as a hard rule for user binaries that still link a semihosting libgloss. The ROI markers are HINT NOPs, so vplat binaries may carry them (`<andesim/ROI.h>`, installed to `build/runtime/include/`) and still run standalone on every engine; binaries you cannot edit delimit the ROI with PC symbols and `--trigger pc` instead.

### vsim CMake Structure

vsim lives entirely in `verilator/`. Key CMake options:
- `VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID` (default OFF) - enables e2e CTest registration
- `VSIM_CONFIG_FILE` - CPU YAML (default `config.yaml`)
- `VSIM_NO_VERILATOR` - skip Verilator build (assume prebuilt)

The hybrid orchestration layer (`src/hybrid/*.hpp`) is header-only and depends only on C++20 standard library + the shared ABI header. SystemC/Verilator are not required for hybrid unit tests.

Hybrid unit tests (`tests/hybrid/`) use [doctest](https://github.com/doctest/doctest). They are registered in `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` and run via `ctest`. The `recording_bus.hpp` pattern provides a duck-typed test double for the DMI bus without requiring virtual interfaces.

## Key Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` | Wire-format struct (shared by all three components) |
| `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | TCG plugin: drain on trigger |
| `verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` | Phase dispatcher |
| `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | DMI state restore (Tier A+B) |
| `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` | DMI state capture |
| `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp` | V register transport via scratch region |
| `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` | CTest registration for all e2e fixtures |
| `scripts/run_e2e.sh` | Parallel e2e runner (FIFO job pool, per-test logs) |
| `tests/fixtures/Makefile` | RISC-V ELF fixture build (Andes toolchain) |

# hybrid_sim

Workspace for the Andes hybrid simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz) + vsim
(SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) sharing memory and architectural state
across a magic-CSR boundary.

Submodule:

- `include/` - the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): the `hybrid_state_v1` wire
  contract under `include/hybrid/`, shared by the plugin, the driver, and vsim.

QEMU and vsim are integrated as prebuilt external binaries (set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` and
`VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env`; see `config.env.example`), not vendored as
submodules. vsim sources live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo, built there.

## Quickstart

```sh
git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim && cd hybrid_sim
./andesim build
./andesim test
```

Subcommands: `list`, `build`, `run`, `test`. Run `./andesim -h` for the
full list. See `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` Section 0.5 for a four-command
worked example, or Sections 1-5 for the developer-grade scripts
(`setup.sh`, `tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`).

## Host dependencies

- C/C++ toolchain (clang preferred), CMake >= 3.20, ninja
- Python 3
- glib-2.0 dev (for the QEMU plugin)
- pkg-config
- Verilator (auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed)
- a prebuilt `qemu-system-riscv64` (external; this repo no longer builds QEMU --
  set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` in `config.env`)
- a prebuilt vsim (external; this repo no longer builds vsim -- set `VSIM_BIN_DIR`
  in `config.env` to your vsim checkout's `build/` dir)

## Outputs

After `./andesim build`:

- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so` (+ `libhotloops.so`)

QEMU and vsim are external prebuilt binaries: `$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64`
and `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*` (set both in `config.env`).

1	# hotloops - hot inner-loop detector
2	
3	Detects the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
4	translation-block transitions in `qemu-system-<arch>`. For each detected
5	loop you get the loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, and the iteration
6	count. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
7	present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.
8	
9	Two parts ship together:
10	
11	- `contrib/plugins/hotloops.c` - QEMU TCG plugin that records edges.
12	- `scripts/hotloops.sh` - wrapper that runs the plugin and formats output.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	```
17	scripts/hotloops.sh [options] <elf>
18	```
19	
20	The wrapper launches `qemu-system-<arch>` with `-bios <elf>` on a baremetal
21	machine (default `andes_ae350`) and a vector-capable CPU (default

# hotloops - hot inner-loop detector

Detects the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
translation-block transitions in `qemu-system-<arch>`. For each detected
loop you get the loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, and the iteration
count. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.

Two parts ship together:

- `contrib/plugins/hotloops.c` - QEMU TCG plugin that records edges.
- `scripts/hotloops.sh` - wrapper that runs the plugin and formats output.

## Usage

```
scripts/hotloops.sh [options] <elf>
```

The wrapper launches `qemu-system-<arch>` with `-bios <elf>` on a baremetal
machine (default `andes_ae350`) and a vector-capable CPU (default
`andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024`). Override per the options below
for other targets.

### Options

| Flag                | Default            | Description                                                    |
|---------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--arch <a>`        | auto               | Target arch: `riscv32`, `riscv64`, or `auto` (from `file`).    |
| `--qemu <path>`     | auto               | Override the `qemu-system-<arch>` binary.                      |
| `--plugin <path>`   | auto               | Override the plugin `.so`.                                     |
| `--machine <name>`  | `andes_ae350`      | `-M <name>` passed to QEMU.                                    |
| `--cpu <spec>`      | `andes-ax45mpv,...`| `-cpu <spec>` passed to QEMU. Default enables RVV 1.0 vlen=1024.|
| `--qemu-config <f>` | -                  | `-readconfig <file>` (e.g. AE350 device cfg).                  |
| `--cwd <dir>`       | -                  | `chdir` before launching QEMU (so semihosting `fread` of `bin/*.bin` resolves). |
| `--qemu-arg <arg>`  | -                  | Extra arg appended to the QEMU command. Repeatable.            |
| `--limit <N>`       | 50                 | Print at most N loops.                                         |
| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1                  | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
| `--objdump <path>`  | auto               | Override objdump (for `function+offset` and disassembly).      |
| `--addr2line <path>`| auto               | Override addr2line (for source-line resolution).               |
| `--no-source`       | off                | Skip source resolution even if DWARF is present.               |
| `--raw`             | off                | Print raw plugin output (CSV-ish), no formatting.              |
| `--optimize-rvv`    | on                 | Only report loops that contain at least one RVV instruction.   |
| `--no-optimize-rvv` | off                | Disable the RVV-only filter; report all loops.                 |
| `--llm`             | on                 | Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption (see below).  |
| `--no-llm`          | off                | Emit the plain human-readable table instead of the LLM report. |

### Build prerequisites

The plugin lives in `contrib/plugins/`. Build once:

```
ninja -C build contrib-plugins
```

It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotloops.c`. The QEMU binaries
themselves (`qemu-system-riscv64`, `qemu-system-riscv32`) do **not** need
to be rebuilt.

## How it detects a loop

For every translated block, the plugin remembers the PC of its last
instruction. When the next-executed block starts at a PC `<=` that
remembered PC, the transition is a backward edge - i.e. a loop iteration.
The pair `(header_pc, tail_pc)` is the key; the count is the number of
iterations.

This catches every loop a real backward branch closes (for/while/do-while,
goto, manually unrolled tails, etc.) without needing to model branch
semantics.

Caveat: each iteration counted is one *taken* backward branch. A loop
that runs N times has N-1 taken backward branches plus one fall-through
on exit, so the reported count is N-1 per call to the enclosing function.

## Output modes

Three output modes, in order of layered post-processing:

1. `--llm` (default on) - Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption.
2. `--no-llm` - plain human-readable table.
3. `--raw` - unformatted plugin output (overrides the above).

### LLM report (default)

The wrapper emits a single Markdown document structured so an LLM (or a
reader skimming top-down) can answer "what is the hottest loop?" from the
first paragraph, then drill down via stable IDs.

Layout:

- Header block: `target`, `total_iters`, `reported_loops`, `min_iters`,
  `rvv_filter`.
- `## TL;DR` paragraph naming the hottest loop, its function and source
  line, percentage of total iterations, RVV vs scalar (with the top-K
  unique vector mnemonics seen), and nesting status.
- One `### L<N>` fact-sheet per reported loop (sorted by iters desc):
  - `iters` and `pc_range` (`0xstart .. 0xend  (size: N B)`).
  - `function` (`fn+0xoff -> fn+0xoff`).
  - `source` (`file:line` or `file:line -> file:line` if the header and
    tail map to different lines).
  - `code` - inline best-effort source snippet read from the path stored
    in DWARF.
  - `rvv` summary plus `rvv_insns:` listing (capped at 8) with each
    `0xpc  mnemonic operands`.
  - `parent` / `children` - stable IDs of containing / contained loops.
    Inferred from PC-range containment, so this captures only
    same-function nesting.
  - `calls` - direct callees inside the loop body (`jal`/`jalr` with a
    statically known target via the `<name>` annotation). Indirect calls
    show as `(indirect)`.

The TL;DR is templated from the same data fields the per-loop blocks use;
no LLM call is made by the script itself.

Limitations:

- Same-function nesting only. A caller's hot loop that calls a callee
  containing its own hot loop will show as two unrelated loops; follow
  `calls:` to bridge.
- `code:` snippets require the source file to be reachable at the
  absolute path stored in DWARF. Cross-compiled or relocated builds may
  fall back to just `file:line`.
- The RVV filter is mnemonic-based: any insn whose mnemonic begins with
  `v<alpha>` (e.g. `vsetvli`, `vle32.v`, `vadd.vv`, `vmul.vv`). Standard
  scalar RISC-V has no such mnemonic, so this is exact in practice.

### Table mode (`--no-llm`)

Header line, then a fixed-width table sorted by `iters` descending:

```
# hot loops (iters >= <threshold>[, RVV-only]), sorted desc, top <K>
iters | start_pc           -> end_pc             | location              | source
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
<n>   | 0x<16-hex>         -> 0x<16-hex>         | <fn>+0x<o> -> <fn>+0x<o> | file:line -> file:line
...
```

Columns:

- `iters`     - taken backward-branch count (sorted desc).
- `start_pc`  - PC of the loop header (the branch target).
- `end_pc`    - PC of the backward branch (the loop tail).
- `location`  - `function+offset -> function+offset` from the ELF symbol
                table. Shows `?` if the address is not inside any sized
                FUNC symbol.
- `source`    - `file:line -> file:line` from DWARF (basenamed).
                Collapsed to a single `file:line` when both ends map to
                the same source line. Only present when the ELF has debug
                info and `--no-source` is not set.

### Raw mode (`--raw`)

Bypasses both the LLM report and the table, printing the unformatted
plugin output:

```
hotloops: <distinct> distinct backward edges, <hot> hot (>= <thr> iters), sorted by iterations desc
start_pc, end_pc, iterations
0x..., 0x..., <n>
...
```

Stable across releases - useful for piping into another tool.

## Example

A doubly-nested loop with an RVV inner body:

```c
/* hotloops_demo.c - baremetal entry */
#include <stdint.h>

__attribute__((noinline))
static int dot_rvv(const int *a, const int *b, int n) {
    int s = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
    return s;
}

void main(void) {
    static int a[64], b[64];
    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = 64 - i; }
    long total = 0;
    for (int outer = 0; outer < 500; outer++)
        total += dot_rvv(a, b, 64);                  /* 64 * 500 inner iters */
    (void)total;
}
```

Build for AE350 with the Andes RISC-V toolchain (or any baremetal
RVV-capable toolchain), then run:

```
$ scripts/hotloops.sh --min-iters 100 --limit 5 build/hotloops_demo.elf
```

LLM-mode output (the default) looks like:

```markdown
# Hotloops Report
target:           hotloops_demo.elf
total_iters:      32000
reported_loops:   1
min_iters:        100
rvv_filter:       on

## TL;DR
Hottest loop is L1 in `dot_rvv` (hotloops_demo.c:6), 31500 iters = 98.4% of
total. Body is RVV (vsetvli, vle32.v, vmul.vv, +1 more). It is top-level
(no parent loop), and contains no inner loop.

## Loops

### L1 [hottest]  (98.4% of total)
iters:        31500
pc_range:     0x80000200 .. 0x80000218  (size: 24 B)
function:     dot_rvv+0x10 -> dot_rvv+0x28
source:       hotloops_demo.c:6
code:         for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
rvv:          yes (4 insns)
rvv_insns:
  - 0x80000200  vsetvli    t0,a2,e32,m1,ta,ma
  - 0x80000208  vle32.v    v1,(a0)
  - 0x8000020c  vmul.vv    v2,v1,v3
  - 0x80000210  vadd.vv    v4,v4,v2
parent:       -
children:     []
calls:        []
```

Reading the report:

- The TL;DR alone identifies the hot path: `dot_rvv` line 6, 98.4% of all
  taken backward branches, RVV-vectorized.
- `iters = 31500` is close to the expected `64 * 500 = 32000`; the missing
  500 are the per-call exits (last iter of `dot_rvv` falls through instead
  of branching back).
- The 500-iter outer loop in `main` was filtered out by `--min-iters 100`.
  It would also have been filtered by the default RVV-only filter since
  `main`'s body is scalar (drop with `--no-optimize-rvv` to see scalar
  loops too).

For piping into a different tool, use `--raw`:

```
$ scripts/hotloops.sh --raw build/hotloops_demo.elf | head
hotloops: 1 distinct backward edges, 1 hot (>= 1 iters), sorted by iterations desc
start_pc, end_pc, iterations
0x0000000080000200, 0x0000000080000218, 31500
```

## Tips

- Strip rarely-interesting startup loops by raising `--min-iters` to a
  value above your background noise floor (e.g. `--min-iters 1000` for a
  workload that runs your hot path millions of times).
- For a very short workload, lower `--min-iters` and raise `--limit`
  to see the full distribution.
- Default settings filter to RVV-containing loops only; pair with
  `--no-optimize-rvv` if you also want to see the scalar hot spots
  (e.g. an outer driver loop wrapping a vectorized kernel).
- For LLM consumption, pipe the default output straight into your prompt
  - the TL;DR is in the first ~10 lines and the per-loop blocks are
  cross-referenceable by their `L<N>` IDs.
- `--raw` is the stable interface for downstream tooling.

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># andesim demo: how many cycles does `hello` take?

`andesim` runs one RISC-V binary on three models with one command:

| Model    | What it is                                      | Speed | Gives you |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------|-------|-----------|
| `fast`   | functional simulation (QEMU)                    | MHz   | program output, instantly |
| `cycle`  | the real Andes core RTL (Verilator)             | kHz   | exact whole-program cycles |
| `hybrid` | `fast` skips ahead, `cycle` measures one region | ~MHz  | exact cycles for the region you mark |

This demo builds one `hello` program and runs it on all three. No engine
knowledge needed: you write C, compile once, and pick a model at run time.</cell id="cell-0">
<cell id="cell-1">import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andesim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)</cell id="cell-1">

working dir: /home/nick/work/andesim

<cell id="cell-2"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 1. Build `hello`

One compile command. The two flags `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`
link the portable runtime, so the same ELF runs on every engine.</cell id="cell-2">
<cell id="cell-3">%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null      # sets HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > hello.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
  printf("hello\n");
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c -o hello.elf

echo "built:"; file hello.elf</cell id="cell-3">

built:


hello.elf: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, UCB RISC-V, RVC, double-float ABI, version 1 (SYSV), staticall

y linked, with debug_info, not stripped

<cell id="cell-4"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 2. Run it fast

`--mode fast` answers "does my program work?" in well under a second.</cell id="cell-4">
<cell id="cell-5">!andesim run --mode fast hello.elf</cell id="cell-5">

hello

<cell id="cell-6"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 3. See which engines are built

`fast` always runs on QEMU, but `cycle` and `hybrid` execute on a specific
RTL core, so you pick one with `--engine`. `andesim list engines` shows
what this repo has built -- the `vsim:*` rows are the cycle-accurate cores
(and `list models` recaps the three models):</cell id="cell-6">
<cell id="cell-7">!andesim list engines</cell id="cell-7">

ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
qemu                   qemu  functional      64    -     -     -   
vsim:ax45mpv_mp2       vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32  
vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32  
vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32  

<cell id="cell-8"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 4. Same binary, cycle accurate

`--mode cycle` runs the same ELF on the real Andes core RTL. No rebuild.
The `cycles simulated` line is the exact whole-program cycle count.

We name one of the engines above with `--engine` (here, `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`):</cell id="cell-8">
<cell id="cell-9">!andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium hello.elf</cell id="cell-9">

Copyright (C) 2013-2026 Andes Technology Corporation. All rights reserved.
Version : unknown



[[32minfo[m] loading segment: addr=0x100000, memsz=37160, filesz=36320
[[32minfo[m] hart 0 reset vector: 0x100000


hello


[[32minfo[m] sim_control: received command 0x0
[[32minfo[m] sim_control: got exit 0, stopping
[[32minfo[m] Exit PC: 100488
[[32minfo[m] Core 0 last PCs: 0x100488 0x10048a 
[[32minfo[m] 3573 cycles simulated
[[32minfo[m] 0.413s elapsed, 8651.332Hz

<cell id="cell-10"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>`hello` finishes in a fraction of a second here, but RTL simulation runs
at kHz: a real workload takes hours this way. And the count includes
everything: boot, runtime setup, exit. Usually you only care about one
region. That is what `hybrid` is for.

## 5. Mark the region you care about

Wrap the region with two markers from `<andesim/ROI.h>` and recompile.
The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions, i.e. NOPs: they cost nothing,
and the marked binary still runs everywhere, even on real silicon.

Here we measure exactly one `printf`:</cell id="cell-10">
<cell id="cell-11">%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > hello.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

int main(void)
{
  andesim_ROI_begin();   /* start measuring here */
  printf("hello\n");
  andesim_ROI_end();     /* stop measuring here */
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c -o hello.elf

echo "rebuilt with markers"
</cell id="cell-11">

rebuilt with markers

<cell id="cell-12"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### Markers are free

The marked binary is still a normal program. On `fast` (or on silicon) the
markers do nothing:</cell id="cell-12">
<cell id="cell-13">!andesim run --mode fast hello.elf</cell id="cell-13">

hello

<cell id="cell-14"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 6. Hybrid: skip ahead fast, measure exactly

`--mode hybrid --trigger marker` runs everything before the first marker
on the fast engine, then hands the live program state to the RTL engine,
which executes the marked region cycle by cycle.</cell id="cell-14">
<cell id="cell-15">!andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium hello.elf</cell id="cell-15">

|---------|--------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| `fast`  | QEMU's built-in GDB stub                   | port `1234`       |

remote_bitbang host localhost

transport select jtag
set _CHIPNAME riscv

init

<cell id="cell-28"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>#### How it works under the hood

GDB never talks to vsim directly — three processes form a chain:

```
GDB --(gdb-remote :1111)--> $ICEMAN / OpenOCD --(JTAG bitbang :9104)--> vsim (RTL)
```

vsim exposes a JTAG **remote-bitbang** port; OpenOCD drives that link, speaks the
RISC-V Debug Module protocol to halt / step / read the hart, and re-exports an
ordinary **gdb-remote** server (port `1111`) — the port GDB actually attaches to.
That is why you point GDB at the server's port, not at vsim's `9104`.

`andesim` wires the three together:

1. Fork `vsim` in the background with `--jtag-port 9104 -S`.
2. Poll until that port is listening — OpenOCD does **not** retry the bitbang
   connect, so launching it before vsim is ready would just fail.
3. `exec $ICEMAN`, which bridges the JTAG link to the gdb-remote port.

The one piece of real machinery is the `-S` halt. `--jtag-port` *alone* leaves
the hart free-running, and a debugger attaching over the passive bitbang link can
never catch a running RTL hart — its `dmstatus` oscillates `running` /
`unavailable` and never reaches `allhalted`. So `--gdb` always pairs `--jtag-port`
with `-S`, which halts the hart **in-process, before the port opens**, over the
same Debug-Module path the hybrid handoff uses (`dmactive -> haltreq -> poll
allhalted`). The debugger then attaches to an already-stopped core, and its first
`continue` issues `resumereq` to begin execution.

Implementation: `run_cycle_gdb` in `driver/cmd_run.cpp` (the orchestration above)
and `Simulator::halt_for_debug` in `verilator/src/simulator.hpp` (the in-process
halt).</cell id="cell-28">

# andesim demo: how many cycles does `hello` take?

`andesim` runs one RISC-V binary on three models with one command:

| Model    | What it is                                      | Speed | Gives you |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------|-------|-----------|
| `fast`   | functional simulation (QEMU)                    | MHz   | program output, instantly |
| `cycle`  | the real Andes core RTL (Verilator)             | kHz   | exact whole-program cycles |

knowledge needed: you write C, compile once, and pick a model at run time.
